extracted.intended_audience: referees/peer reviewers for the Journal of Finance (academic finance researchers serving as referees)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing single-blind referee reports for submissions to the Journal of Finance, including report structure, decision-relevant criteria, tone expectations, AI use policy, and confidentiality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review type (single-blind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refereeing at The Journal of Finance (JF) is single-blind — referees know author identities but authors do not know referee identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural rule about anonymity that affects conflicts of interest and how referees should treat author-identifying information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of refereeing
rubrics_metrics.description: Help editor make a decision; Help authors improve their work; Maintain the quality of published research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three purposes should guide the content and tone of the report: provide decision-useful evaluation for editors, actionable feedback for authors, and uphold scholarly standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief synopsis — what the paper does, in your own words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start the report with a concise restatement of the paper's aims, approach, and main findings so the editor (and authors) can quickly see you understood the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of the contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of the contribution — why it matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the paper's contribution relative to the literature and why the topic is important; place the work in context rather than only describing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major issues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and explain substantive, potentially fatal flaws or large gaps (e.g., credibility of identification, essential methodological problems) that materially affect the paper's publishability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor issues — specific suggestions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List smaller, fixable items (clarifications, presentation, additional robustness checks that are reasonable) intended to help the authors improve the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to the editor — the referee's decision recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear recommendation (e.g., accept, revise, reject) for the editor, supported by the evaluation in the report. The report should primarily help the editor decide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the research question addresses a meaningful problem for the literature or practice; importance affects the priority for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate novelty of the idea, contribution, or approach relative to existing literature; distinguish incremental versus substantially new advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of analysis: Is the methodology sound?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the correctness and appropriateness of theoretical models, empirical methods, econometric techniques, and implementation; point out errors or weaknesses in inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification (empirical strategy credibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification: Is the empirical strategy credible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the identification assumptions are plausible, whether the causal interpretation is justified, and whether threats to identification are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Robustness: Have alternative explanations been ruled out?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for alternative hypotheses, sensitivity analyses, robustness checks, and whether results hold under reasonable variations; recommend additional checks when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory–data fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Theory-data fit: Do the empirical results match the theoretical predictions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate consistency between the theoretical framework and empirical findings; note mismatches and whether theory or interpretation should be revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing quality: Is the paper clearly presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity, organization, and readability; flag confusing exposition, unclear notation, or poor structure that impede understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive tone and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be constructive: Even if you recommend rejection, your report should help the authors improve their work. Avoid personal attacks, vague criticisms, demanding citations of your own work, and suggesting unrealistically extensive new analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional, actionable feedback. Anti-patterns to avoid include personal attacks, unsupported or vague criticism, self-serving citation demands, and requests for unrealistic additional work.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use policy for referees
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of AI software may be employed in the preparation of referee reports to assist with drafting or editing text or looking up prior references. However, referees remain fully responsible for the content of their reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees may use AI tools for drafting/editing or literature lookup, but must verify and take responsibility for accuracy, originality, and confidentiality of report content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal has strict confidentiality policies regarding the peer review process and referee identities. Manuscripts are privileged communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality of manuscript contents and author identities; do not disclose or share privileged material. Treat submissions as privileged and avoid any breaches that could reveal referee identity or manuscript content.
